notes: Cats: Italy in the Régionale bank (61 stems, 4 of them Lombardy and Emilia-Romagna, plus i-soo2ytq5 on frizzante and spumante and the national law stems shared by every Italian subject) and Italy North in the Village bank (62 stems, 10 of them Lombard or Emilian); Sparkling Wine World is left out of the cats because its 22 stems are mostly Champagne, Cava and Prosecco, though two of its Lambrusco stems are counted in the review. Chapters: the Régionale chapter lombardy, which teaches both regions; the Village chapter Italy North (facts 2 and 6, Chiavennasca and Franciacorta) and Sparkling Wine World, whose facts 2 and 6 are the only Village chapter lines on Lambrusco in tank and on the Franciacorta lees ladder. Region: the lombardy article; Emilia-Romagna has no article of its own, so the country door carries it. Country: italy for the Lambrusco grape line, the label words Secco, Abboccato, Amabile and Dolce, and the DOC ladder. Grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc (as the Régionale profile prints Pinot Bianco) and Pinot Noir for Franciacorta, Nebbiolo for Chiavennasca; Lambrusco has no profile. Techniques: traditional method for Franciacorta, tank method for most Lambrusco, ancestral method for the Lambrusco the Court says may be Methode Ancestrale, dried grapes for Sforzato and the Lombard passito. Service tables: sparkling for the Court's own service standards cell, glassware for the flute or wine glass, temperatures for serving Lambrusco cold.
